# Migrate to Amazon S3

@include "@global/vagrant-eol.mdx"

This guide walks you through moving your Vagrant boxes from HCP Vagrant Registry
to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) and referencing them from a
Vagrantfile. Using the Amazon Web Services (AWS) command line interface (CLI),
you create a bucket, upload your boxes, and optionally serve them publicly.

## Overview

Amazon S3 organizes data into buckets. A bucket is a container that lives in an
AWS Region and holds objects, such as your `vagrant.box` files. Each object has a
key that acts as its unique path within the bucket. In this guide, you create one
bucket and upload your boxes as objects.

## Cost considerations

Amazon S3 is a paid service, so review the pricing model before you migrate your
boxes to understand the charges you may incur. Billing spans several dimensions:

- **Storage.** You pay for the amount of data you store, charged per gigabyte per
  month. The rate depends on the storage class you choose, such as S3 Standard.
- **Requests.** You pay for requests against your objects, such as the `PUT`
  requests you make when you upload boxes and the `GET` requests Vagrant makes
  when it downloads them.
- **Data transfer.** You pay for data transferred out of AWS to the internet,
  such as when users download boxes from a public bucket. Data transfer into S3
  is free.

New AWS accounts include a Free Tier that covers a limited amount of storage,
requests, and data transfer each month. For current rates and Free Tier limits,
refer to the [Amazon S3 pricing page](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/). To
estimate your costs, use the
[AWS Pricing Calculator](https://calculator.aws/#/addService/S3).

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, complete the following:

- Download the boxes you want to migrate from HCP Vagrant Registry so that you
  have the `vagrant.box` files available locally.
- Create an [AWS account](https://aws.amazon.com/resources/create-account/).

## Install the AWS CLI

Install the AWS CLI by following the
[AWS CLI installation guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html).

## Configure credentials and a Region

Configure the CLI with your credentials and a default Region:

```shell-session
$ aws configure
```

The command prompts you for an access key ID, a secret access key, a default
Region, and a default output format. To create an access key, refer to
[Manage access keys for IAM users](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_access-keys.html).

The AWS CLI supports many additional authentication methods, such as AWS IAM
Identity Center and named profiles. Refer to the
[AWS CLI configuration guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-chap-configure.html)
for the full list.

## Create a bucket

Start by creating a bucket to hold your boxes:

```shell-session
$ aws s3api create-bucket --bucket BUCKET_NAME --region REGION --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=REGION
```

Bucket names must be globally unique across all AWS accounts. If you create the
bucket in the `us-east-1` Region, omit the `--create-bucket-configuration`
option, because that Region does not accept a location constraint.

For more options, refer to
[create-bucket](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3api/create-bucket.html).

## Upload a box

With the bucket in place, upload a box into it. Use `--key` to set the object path
within the bucket and `--body` to point to the local `vagrant.box` file. Pass
`--region` to target the Region where you created the bucket:

```shell-session
$ aws s3api put-object --bucket BUCKET_NAME --key KEY --body PATH_TO_BOX --region REGION
```

If you omit `--region`, the CLI uses the default Region from your
`aws configure` settings.

For example, a `KEY` like `BOX_NAME/VERSION/PROVIDER/ARCHITECTURE/vagrant.box`
keeps your boxes organized by version, provider, and architecture. For more upload
options, refer to
[put-object](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3api/put-object.html).

## Make the bucket public

Buckets are private by default. To let Vagrant download boxes without
authentication, you allow public access to the objects in the bucket.

The approach below is one way to make the bucket public. It applies a
least-privilege configuration that grants anonymous read-only access through a
bucket policy while keeping access-control list (ACL) based public access
blocked. Depending on your needs, you can choose other approaches and adjust the
level of restriction. For example, you can scope the policy to a prefix instead
of the whole bucket, restrict access by IP range or other conditions, serve boxes
through Amazon CloudFront instead of exposing the bucket directly, or grant access
to specific principals rather than the public. Refer to
[Blocking public access to your Amazon S3 storage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-control-block-public-access.html)
and [Bucket policy examples](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-bucket-policies.html)
to decide what fits your case.

First, keep the settings that block public ACLs enabled, and disable only the
settings that block public bucket policies. This ensures the only public access
comes from the bucket policy you attach next, not from object ACLs:

```shell-session
$ aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket BUCKET_NAME --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=false,RestrictPublicBuckets=false --region REGION
```

Then attach a bucket policy that grants public read access to the objects. The
policy allows only the `s3:GetObject` action, so the public can download boxes
but cannot list, upload, overwrite, or delete them:

```shell-session
$ aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket BUCKET_NAME --region REGION --policy '{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "PublicReadGetObject",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "s3:GetObject",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::BUCKET_NAME/*"
    }
  ]
}'
```

For more details, refer to
[put-bucket-policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3api/put-bucket-policy.html).

~> **Warning:** A public bucket allows anyone to download its objects. Only make
a bucket public if the boxes it contains are safe to distribute publicly. Every
public download also incurs data transfer charges on your account, so a widely
shared or high-traffic box can lead to unexpected costs.

## Reference a box from a public bucket

For a public bucket, the object link has the following form:

```text
https://BUCKET_NAME.s3.REGION.amazonaws.com/KEY
```

Reference the box in your Vagrantfile with `config.vm.box_url`:

```ruby
Vagrant.configure("2") do |config|
  config.vm.box = "BOX_NAME"
  config.vm.box_url = "AWS_S3_URL"
end
```

## Reference a box from a private bucket

For a private bucket, the box is not available at a public URL, so download it
first and add it to Vagrant locally.

Download the box object from the bucket, passing the object's `--key` and the
local file name to save it as. Pass `--region` to target the Region where you
created the bucket:

```shell-session
$ aws s3api get-object --bucket BUCKET_NAME --key KEY LOCAL_FILE --region REGION
```

For more download options, refer to
[get-object](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3api/get-object.html).

Add the downloaded box to Vagrant under a name of your choice:

```shell-session
$ vagrant box add BOX_NAME LOCATION
```

`LOCATION` is the path to the box file you downloaded in the previous step. For
more options, refer to
[vagrant box add](/vagrant/docs/cli/box#box-add).

After you add the box, reference it directly in your Vagrantfile by name:

```ruby
Vagrant.configure("2") do |config|
  config.vm.box = "BOX_NAME"
end
```
